I'm certainly not an expert in the differential geometry part of the library, so please excuse my basic questions. I'm looking for review but I can confirm that all the code below is not AI-written :-)

1) Is this how we say "let X be a compact Riemann surface" in Lean? (for me Riemann surfaces are connected (and hence nonempty)):

import Mathlib

open scoped ContDiff -- for ω notation

-- since when did I not have to write `universe u`?

variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X]
  [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) ω X]

2) Is this how to say "let f:X→Yf:X\to Yf:X→Y be a holomorphic map between two such Riemann surfaces"? 

import Mathlib

open scoped ContDiff

variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X]
  [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) ω X]

variable {Y : Type v} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] [CompactSpace Y] [ConnectedSpace Y]
  [ChartedSpace ℂ Y] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) ω Y]

open scoped Manifold -- for C^n notation

variable (f : C^ω⟮(modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ), X; (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ), Y⟯)

3) I am assuming that we do not have the definition of the degree of such a map (the
degree of a constant map could be 0, and it's a theorem that there's a sensible notion
of degree for a nonconstant map of compact Riemann surfaces). Do we have
the field of meromorphic functions on a compact Riemann surface? This would be another
way of defining degree.

4) Do we have a construction of the 2-sphere as a 1-dimensional complex manifold?

5) Can we talk about the space of global holomorphic 1-forms on a compact Riemann surface yet? (this would lead to a definition of genus). Actually don't we have singular homology with coefficients in Z\ZZ? So perhaps this would be another route to a definition of twice the genus :-)

6) In the docstring for Geometry/Manifold/Diffeomorph it claims

* `Diffeomorph I I' M M' n`: `n`-times continuously differentiable diffeomorphism between
  `M` and `M'` with respect to I and I'; we do not introduce a separate definition for the case
  `n = ∞` or `n = ω`; we use notation instead.

But I can't find the notation for n = ω (at least in that file). Is there notation for this? Should I be using n = ω for developing a theory of compact Riemann surfaces anyway?

Good questions! Some answers:
(1) You might be better off using docs#EuclideanSpace as model space. I'm not sure if it's nicer to speak about smooth or analytic maps (which are mathematically equivalent IIRC).
(2) That's the bundled version; differential geometry usually uses unbundled objects. In this case, you'd use docs#ContMDiff as in {f : X → X} (hf : CMDiff ω f). (Perhaps your eventual theorems concern bundled objects, but you'll find mind API is about the unbundled ones under the hood --- so I highly recommend working with those most of the time.)
Again, the question if complex differentiable, complex smooth or complex analytic is the best to work with. This might depend on your particular question.
(3) Indeed, that degree is missing. Would be nice to add! (My research agenda in any application lists that as a basic missing ingredient. Be my guest :-))
(4) We have docs#EuclideanSpace.instIsManifoldSphere, i.e. the sphere (in a real inner product space) as a real analytic manifold. Not as a complex manifold yet.

(5) As a symplectic topologist, I would prefer the singular homology route --- cheering on anybody who needs cheering to finally get the homology of spheres into mathlib :-)
Handle attaching, i.e. being able to state that classification, is not very far away - but not quite there yet either.

I think n=ω is technically overkill here. n=1 will work fine since it is a standard result of Complex Analysis that complex differentiable implies analytic. This could potentially make some theorems easier to prove, but of course both formulations are mathematically equivalent.

Regarding the question about holomorphic 1-forms, no there are not currently any differential forms in Mathlib. But @Yury G. Kudryashov currently has a construction of the alternating bundle in #35985, which will naturally give rise to differential forms as smooth sections. I believe his construction is general enough that it should yield holomorphic forms just by setting 𝕜=ℂ.
We surely don't need any alternating anything if we're just doing one dimension.

Ah right, of course, my mistake. For 1-forms we just need sections of the Cotangent bundle. That isn't currently in Mathlib as an explicit definition, but it can be easily implemented as Hom(TangentSpace, Trivial) using the existing Hom bundles. I believe something like this would work:

import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic
import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.SmoothSection
import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Tangent
import Mathlib.Topology.VectorBundle.Hom

noncomputable section

namespace Bundle

variable (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {B : Type*}
variable (E : B → Type*) [∀ x, AddCommGroup (E x)] [∀ x, Module 𝕜 (E x)]
  [∀ x, TopologicalSpace (E x)]

/-- Defining the dual of vector bundle -/
abbrev dual : B → Type _ :=
  fun x => E x →L[𝕜] Bundle.Trivial B 𝕜 x

end Bundle

open scoped Manifold ContDiff

universe u

/-- Same assumptions you made for Riemann surface -/
variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X]
  [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) ω X]

private abbrev I := modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ

abbrev CotangentSpace (x : X) := Bundle.dual ℂ (TangentSpace I) x

/-- The cotangent bundle over a complex manifold -/
def CotangentBundle := Bundle.TotalSpace (ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) (Bundle.dual ℂ (TangentSpace I : X → Type _))

/-- A holomorphic 1-form -/
def OneForm := Cₛ^1⟮I; ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ, (CotangentSpace : X → Type _)⟯

end
Thanks! I'll have to spend some time understanding this code. Can you make them into a complex vector space?

Well the Cotangent bundle defined above should already be a complex vector space at each point, since by the definition CotangentSpace x unfolds into TangentSpace I x →L[ℂ] Bundle.Trivial B ℂ x, which is definitionally equal to ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ. That is, the (complex) dual vector space of ℂ.

As for the space of OneForms themselves, the lemmas ContMDiff.smul_section and ContMDiff.add_section in Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/SmoothSection guarantee that they form a module over the holomorphic functions X → ℂ. Also, given any e : Trivialization (ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) π a local trivialization of the cotangent bundle and a basis b for ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ (e.g. the canonical basis dz) we can call e.localFrame b to get the smooth local section dz. Then given a ω : OneForm, we can use contMDiffAt_localFrame_coeff to get the smooth coefficients of ω with respect to this frame. So locally we can write ω = f(z) dz for some holomorphic function f. Is this what you meant?
What I mean is "can you write code to make the correct term of type Module \C (OneForm X)"

import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic
import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.SmoothSection
import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Tangent
import Mathlib.Topology.VectorBundle.Hom

noncomputable section

namespace Bundle

variable (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {B : Type*}
variable (E : B → Type*) [∀ x, AddCommGroup (E x)] [∀ x, Module 𝕜 (E x)]
  [∀ x, TopologicalSpace (E x)]

abbrev dual : B → Type _ :=
  fun x => E x →L[𝕜] Bundle.Trivial B 𝕜 x

end Bundle

open scoped Manifold ContDiff

universe u

private abbrev I := modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ

variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X]
  [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [IsManifold I ω X]

abbrev CotangentSpace (x : X) := Bundle.dual ℂ (TangentSpace I) x

def CotangentBundle := Bundle.TotalSpace (ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) (Bundle.dual ℂ (TangentSpace I : X → Type _))

/-! ### 1-forms -/

/-- A holomorphic 1-form -/
def OneForm := Cₛ^1⟮I; ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ, (CotangentSpace : X → Type _)⟯

namespace OneForm

/-- 1-forms are an additive, commutative group -/
instance instAddCommGroup : AddCommGroup (OneForm (X := X)) :=
  ContMDiffSection.instAddCommGroup

/-- 1-forms are a module over `ℂ` -/
instance instModule : Module ℂ (OneForm (X := X)) :=
  ContMDiffSection.instModule

end OneForm

/-- The genus of a compact Riemann surface is the dimension of its space of holomorphic 1-forms. -/
def genus : ℕ := Module.finrank ℂ (OneForm (X := X))

end

Weiyi Wang said:

Do we even have the Field of meromorphic functions on ℂ? I remember it was mentioned as a roadblock in a Lean Together talk because of junk values at poles

I believe this was solved by @Stefan Kebekus and others

The folder Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic implements basic meromorphic functions. But it does not implement Field on meromorphic functions. The existing implementation also only works on ℂ^nsince it assumes the underlying domain is a NormedSpace. We would need to define something like MeromorphicM for manifolds, analogous to ContMDiff for ContDiff.

The main result is toMeromorphicNFOn which shows that any meromorphic function f can locally be written like f(z) = g(z) / (z-p)^n at any pole p of order n, for some nonvanishing holomorphic g(z). I don't think there is much beyond that though.

I believe the main obstruction to Field is that we can not actually prove the field axiom f * f⁻¹ = 1 since this equality does not hold pointwise. Namely, if f has a pole/zero at z then (f / f) z = 0 as a junk value. The theorem toMeromorphicNFOn I stated above is not technically correct, it requires modifying f by some discrete set of points.

What we really need to do is to define germs of meromorphisms: an equivalence class [f] of functions that differ only on a discrete set of points. It should then be possible to implement Field on the space of those germs. But it is not currently in Mathlib.

Weiyi Wang schrieb:

Do we even have the Field of meromorphic functions on ℂ? I remember it was mentioned as a roadblock in a Lean Together talk because of junk values at poles

The Field of meromorphic functions on ℂ. Fixing this is definitively on my TODO-List, and if the need arises, I am very willing to move the item up on the list. My plan is to have two flavors of meromorphic functions.

  • Meromorphic functions, the functions. These are honest functions, that do however not form a field (observe that the function x/x is not continuous). In fact, if f is meromorphic, and g agrees with f outside a discrete set, then g is again meromorphic.
  • Meromorphic functios, the field. Similar to what has been done for L^p-spaces, this is the quotient (functions)/(eventually equal wrt to codiscrete filter). This quotient gives a field, but its members are not functions anymore, so operations like contour integration are not defined. Continuous extension gives a section (field) -> (functions), but note that this is NOT a ring morphism.

Can't you still define the contour integral with coercion (by picking a random representative)? It sounds to me that it is exactly the same construction with just a different proposition and filter, no?

@Jack McCarthy I am late to the party but I scribbled this down some time ago

import Mathlib

open Set Bundle ContDiff Manifold Trivialization

variable
  {B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace B]
  {EB : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup EB] [NormedSpace ℝ EB]
  {HB : Type*} [TopologicalSpace HB]
  {IB : ModelWithCorners ℝ EB HB}
  [ChartedSpace HB B]

variable
  {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  {E : B → Type*}
  [∀ x, NormedAddCommGroup (E x)]
  [∀ x, NormedSpace ℝ (E x)]
  [TopologicalSpace (TotalSpace F E)]
  [FiberBundle F E]
  [VectorBundle ℝ F E]

noncomputable section

/-- A vector field is a smooth section of the tangent bundle -/
def VectorField := Cₛ^∞⟮IB; F, E⟯


/-- A 1-form is a smooth section of the dual bundle -/
def OneForm := Cₛ^∞⟮IB; F →L[ℝ] ℝ, fun b ↦ E b →L[ℝ] ℝ⟯

def apply
  (w : OneForm (E := E) (F := F) (IB := IB))
  (X : VectorField (IB := IB) (E := E) (F := F)) (b : B) : ℝ :=
    w.toFun b (X.toFun b)

lemma apply_smooth
  (w : OneForm (E := E) (F := F) (IB := IB))
  (X : VectorField (IB := IB) (E := E) (F := F)) :
  ContMDiff IB (IB.prod 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ)) ∞
      (fun b ↦ TotalSpace.mk' ℝ b (w.toFun b (X.toFun b))) :=
  (ContMDiffSection.contMDiff w).clm_bundle_apply
      (ContMDiffSection.contMDiff X)

#check ContMDiff.clm_bundle_apply₂

lemma apply_smooth'
  (w : OneForm (E := E) (F := F) (IB := IB))
  (X : VectorField (IB := IB) (E := E) (F := F)) :
  ContMDiff IB 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (apply w X) := by
  intro b
  have h := (apply_smooth w X).contMDiffAt (x := b)
  rw [Trivialization.contMDiffAt_iff (e := trivializationAt ℝ (Trivial B ℝ) b) (by simp)] at h
  simpa using h.2

lemma apply_smooth''
  (w : OneForm (E := E) (F := F) (IB := IB))
  (X : VectorField (IB := IB) (E := E) (F := F)) :
  ContMDiff IB 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (fun b ↦ w.toFun b (X.toFun b)) := by
  intro b
  have h1 := (apply_smooth w X).contMDiffAt (x := b)
  have h2 :
    TotalSpace.mk' ℝ b ((w.toFun b) (X.toFun b)) ∈ (trivializationAt ℝ (Trivial B ℝ) b).source :=
      by simp
  have h3 := Trivialization.contMDiffAt_iff
             (n := ∞) (IB := IB) (IM := IB)
             (f := fun b ↦ TotalSpace.mk' ℝ b ((w.toFun b) (X.toFun b)))
             (e := trivializationAt ℝ (Trivial B ℝ) b) h2
  rw [h3] at h1
  have h6 : ContMDiffAt IB 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞
    (fun x ↦ ((trivializationAt ℝ (Trivial B ℝ) b)
              ((fun c ↦ TotalSpace.mk' ℝ c ((w.toFun c) (X.toFun c))) x)).2) b := h1.2
  have h4 : ∀ x,
    ((trivializationAt ℝ (Trivial B ℝ) b) (TotalSpace.mk' ℝ x ((w.toFun x) (X.toFun x)))).2 =
    (w.toFun x) (X.toFun x) := fun x ↦ by
      simp [Trivial.fiberBundle_trivializationAt', Trivial.trivialization_apply]
  have h5 : ContMDiffWithinAt IB 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (fun x ↦ (w.toFun x) (X.toFun x)) univ b :=
  ContMDiffWithinAt.congr h1.2 (fun x _ ↦ (h4 x).symm) (h4 b).symm
  exact h5

-- Principal bundle total space
variable
  {P : Type*} [TopologicalSpace P]
  {EP : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup EP] [NormedSpace ℝ EP]
  {HP : Type*} [TopologicalSpace HP]
  {IP : ModelWithCorners ℝ EP HP}
  [ChartedSpace HP P]
  [IsManifold IP ∞ P]
  {FP : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup FP] [NormedSpace ℝ FP]

def LieAlgebraValuedOneForm (G : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
    [LieRing G] [LieAlgebra ℝ G] :=
  Cₛ^∞⟮IP; FP →L[ℝ] G, fun _p : P ↦ FP →L[ℝ] G⟯

#check LieAlgebra.ad
#check MulAut.conj
